findings.title: `float: right` on .small-action button is ignored once .small-action becomes a flex container
findings.body: `.small-action` is now `display: flex` (via `@include flexbox()`), which makes `.topic-avatar`, `.small-action-desc` and `button` flex items. Per the flexbox spec, `float` has no effect on flex items, so the `button { float: right; }` rule at line 309 no longer pushes the action button to the right edge. The button will now sit immediately after the description text instead of being right-aligned, which is a visible layout regression for small-action posts (e.g. closed/pinned/moved notices with controls). To keep the previous placement the button needs `margin-left: auto` (or `.small-action-desc` needs `flex: 1`).

findings.title: order() mixin passes the same value to -webkit-box-ordinal-group, which is 1-based unlike `order`
findings.body: `-webkit-box-ordinal-group` (legacy 2009 flexbox) defaults to 1 and is 1-based, while the standard `order` property defaults to 0. Passing the same `$val` to both means that in legacy-WebKit browsers an item with `order(2)` is given ordinal-group 2 while untouched siblings are at ordinal-group 1, whereas in modern browsers the untouched siblings are at 0. This happens to work for the current usages (2 and 3 are both > default) but the mixin is not a faithful polyfill; a caller using `order(1)` to move an element after its siblings would get no effect in legacy WebKit. Either document the limitation or emit `$val + 1` for the ordinal-group property.

findings.title: align-items() mixin does not translate values for legacy -webkit-box-align / -ms-flex-align, and emits a non-existent -ms-align-items
findings.body: The legacy properties `-webkit-box-align` and `-ms-flex-align` use `start`/`end` rather than `flex-start`/`flex-end`, so forwarding `$alignment` unchanged produces invalid declarations for those values (only `center`, `baseline` and `stretch` coincide). `-ms-align-items` is not a property any IE version ever supported and is dead output. Current call sites only use `center` and `baseline`, so nothing breaks today, but the mixin silently fails for other arguments; it should map the values or restrict accepted inputs.

findings.title: PR title claims a performance optimization but the change is a float-to-flexbox layout rewrite
findings.body: The PR is titled "Optimize header layout performance with flexbox mixins" and its description is just "Test 5". Nothing in the diff is a performance change: it replaces `float: left/right` on `.title`/`.panel` with a flex container on `.d-header .contents`, reorders `.extra-info-wrapper` via `order(2)`, removes the `.badge-wrapper.bullet` top margin in the header, and restyles `.small-action` spacing. These are user-visible layout changes with browser-support implications (flexbox requires IE10+), and reviewers/theme authors relying on the title will be misled. The title and description should accurately describe the layout change and any intended visual differences.
